title: Context engineering for AI agents
summary: Microsoft beginner lesson on context engineering for agents: scratchpads, memory, summarization, poisoning, tool overload.

assertions.quote: ensuring our AI agent has the right information at the right time

verdicts.note: As models improved, output depends more on relevant, high-signal context than phrasing; consistent with Anthropic/Cursor guidance and long-context degradation evidence.

assertions.quote: this information can stay out of the context window and is only called when needed

verdicts.note: External notes/memory files are a standard, effective pattern (Anthropic, Manus write-ups) for long tasks; adds retrieval overhead.

assertions.quote: compressing context ... summarizing the context as it grows ... or pruning

verdicts.note: Summarization cuts cost and keeps sessions going, but lossy summaries can drop details that matter; quality depends on what is kept.

assertions.quote: context poisoning ... validate information before it enters the context

verdicts.note: Errors in context are re-used by later turns; validating tool outputs before storing them is standard agent hygiene.

MLR codes 'cumulative context errors and iteration drift' (2 of 47 sources): misunderstandings from earlier prompts propagate and WL15 reports successive prompts amplifying earlier errors; the validate-before-context remedy is not tested.

assertions.quote: it ends up choosing the wrong one due to the number of tools

verdicts.note: Tool-selection accuracy drops as tool count grows (e.g. Berkeley function-calling and RAG-MCP results); dynamic tool loadouts help.
